title: Building a 36k-province grand strategy game with Claude Code: what the workflow looks like
author: Necessary_Weekend896
selftext:
i've been making ruler of the seven climes, a grand strategy game on the real world map (36,000 provinces, 190+ countries, starts from 1444 to 2026). free in the browser. i do the design, the decisions and the playtesting; claude code writes the code and most of the content.

my loop is basically:

1. play a session and write down what feels wrong as plain observations ("my manpower stays at zero after i demobilize", "the AI's air force is huge compared to its army")
2. claude traces it in the code, explains the cause, fixes it and adds a test
3. claude runs headless simulations of a few in-game years to check the numbers (that's how we measured the AI going from 1,164 to 2,568 planes in peacetime)
4. i playtest the new build and the cycle repeats

the hardest part has been things you can only judge by playing, like how the map feels when you pan, or whether a peace deal feels fair. claude can measure, but it can't feel the lag on my laptop, so i'm the one who has to catch those.

curious how others handle playtesting and feedback with AI. do you write bug reports for it, or let it play the game itself?

[https://saasse.itch.io/ruler-of-the-seven-climes](https://saasse.itch.io/ruler-of-the-seven-climes)

replies.author: Necessary_Weekend896
replies.body: hey, thanks for asking! right now the game isn't on android, but it runs in the browser on mobile devices too. if the audience grows i'll definitely bring it to android, ios and pc. also, there's only a flag editor at the moment, but a scenario editor could be added. i'd love to hear any other thoughts or ideas you have about the game :)
